bottom_line: Prasinezumab — PASADENA / PADOVA. Stated failure: Phase II/IIb: primary endpoints missed; PADOVA p=0.0657. Diagnosis (claim 1.1, supported): PADOVA's primary endpoint was time to confirmed motor progression event assessed by MDS-UPDRS Part III; prasinezumab narrowly missed it with HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.01, p=0.0657) versus placebo.
lines: [1] PADOVA's primary endpoint was time to confirmed motor progression event assessed by MDS-UPDRS Part III; prasinezumab narrowly missed it with HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.01, p=0.0657) versus placebo. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[2] The curated record states PASADENA missed its global primary measure and PADOVA later narrowly missed its primary endpoint. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[3] PASADENA exploratory analyses suggested greater motor effects in faster progressors, and PADOVA had supportive trends and a nominal signal in a prespecified levodopa subgroup; this is development continuation/redesign evidence, not a demonstrated clinical rescue. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: hypothesis-generating; evidence strength: strong; check: hypothesis-generating).

[4] The PADOVA levodopa subgroup was prespecified, so it should not be described as a purely post hoc finding. (section: Failure Diagnosis; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: prespecified; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[5] PADOVA's primary endpoint was time to confirmed motor progression event assessed by MDS-UPDRS Part III; prasinezumab showed no significant benefit versus placebo (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.01, p=0.0657). (section: Candidate Responder Population; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

(section: Related Indications; sources: curated record, ClinicalTrials.gov, MONDO; record types: curated, registry, database; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[8] Prasinezumab interacts with alpha-synuclein. (section: Related Indications; sources: ChEMBL; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[9] Prasinezumab was tested in PASADENA (NCT03100149) and PADOVA (NCT04777331), which studied Parkinson disease. (section: Related Indications; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[10] PADOVA narrowly missed its primary endpoint: time to confirmed motor progression event assessed by MDS-UPDRS Part III had HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.01, p=0.0657), just above conventional significance. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: ClinicalTrials.gov; record types: registry; evidence status: registry record; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

[12] PASADENA exploratory analyses suggested greater motor effects in faster progressors; PADOVA had supportive trends and a nominal signal in a prespecified levodopa subgroup. (section: Evidence-Supported Redesign Options; sources: curated record; record types: curated; evidence status: curated summary; evidence strength: strong; check: supported by its cited records).

question: Why did prasinezumab miss its primary endpoints in PASADENA and PADOVA, and which patients might still respond?
raw: Prasinezumab missed primary endpoints in PASADENA and narrowly missed in PADOVA [1][2]. PADOVA’s primary endpoint—time to confirmed motor progression by MDS-UPDRS Part III—yielded HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.69–1.01, p=0.0657), just above conventional significance [1][5]. Secondary motor outcomes were non-significant [6]. Curated exploratory analyses suggest greater motor effects in faster progressors and a nominal signal in a prespecified levodopa subgroup [3][4][12], but these are hypothesis-generating, not demonstrated rescue [3]. Lines do not show why PASADENA failed, subgroup effect sizes, or predictive biomarkers.
